subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class quota-bucket/project identity to provider key/profile routing, or keep the current flat key/profile rotation model and handle project-aware pooling outside core for now?
rationale: The remaining request adds new config/state semantics and decides whether bucket cooldown belongs in core auth routing, the Google provider, a plugin API, or an external sidecar; current source does not make that product boundary clear.

options.title: Design generic provider-pool buckets
options.body: Keep this issue open and resolve bucket identity, cooldown scope, docs, and migration behavior as part of a generic provider-pool routing design.

options.title: Limit core to flat rotation
options.body: Document the current key/profile rotation behavior as the supported core contract and leave project-aware pooling to external tools or provider plugins.

options.title: Split to narrower follow-ups
options.body: Close or supersede only after a maintainer creates a canonical bucket-design issue and links the existing auth-profile and cron guardrail overlaps there.

recommendation.title: Design generic provider-pool buckets
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and resolve bucket identity, cooldown scope, docs, and migration behavior as part of a generic provider-pool routing design.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main provider/auth rotation files and recent refactor history point here as the best available routing owner for the product/API decision.
